//: Web verification gates for the Flutter web build. Run with `make verify-web` (build + `npx vlmkit gates run`). See docs/vlmkit.md for why the server is not a plain static file server and why three integrity rules are switched off.

webServer.//: tools/vlmkit/serve-web.mjs serves app/build/web and injects the four lines that enable Flutter's accessibility DOM. A plain static server would serve the same files and every DOM gate would measure an empty page.

rules.//: The accessibility DOM is a description of the canvas, not a rendering of it: Flutter marks it `filter: opacity(0%)` and paints the real pixels into the canvas. Every rule that reads computed paint therefore reports the app as invisible text at 1.00:1. The rules that read geometry, roles, names and state stay on.

check.integrity/invisible-text.reason: Flutter web paints the app into a canvas and renders the accessibility DOM transparent by construction; this rule reports all 8 text blocks on the home screen as invisible at 1.00:1. Use check a11y touch / focus / scan handlers / verify flow, which read roles, names, rects and state.

check.integrity/low-contrast-text.reason: Same cause as invisible-text: the computed fill of every text node is rgba(0,0,0,0) over the page background. Real contrast lives in the Flutter theme and cannot be measured from this DOM.

check.integrity/occluded-text.reason: Same cause: paint order is the canvas's, and hit testing against the transparent accessibility layer says nothing about what a user sees.
